attributes.name: [OpenRouter] Model Latency Regression
attributes.description: Alerts when the p99 end-to-end latency for any model exceeds a configurable threshold. Detects model or provider degradation before it impacts end-user experience. Works with the default dimensions (model, api_key_id). To alert per provider instead, add 'provider' to the performance stream dimensions.

investigation_guide.blob:
## Model Latency Regression

### Triage Steps
1. Open the OpenRouter Performance dashboard and inspect the p99 latency trend per model.
2. Identify which model is degraded:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | WHERE @timestamp > NOW() - 3 HOURS | STATS p99 = MAX(openrouter.performance.p99_latency) BY openrouter.performance.model | SORT p99 DESC`
3. Check whether the affected model also shows lower throughput:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | STATS tput = AVG(openrouter.performance.p50_throughput) BY openrouter.performance.model`
4. Consider switching to a different model or provider via OpenRouter's fallback routing.

### Common Causes
- Provider-side capacity constraints or incidents
- Large model deployment rollout at the provider
- Network congestion between OpenRouter and the provider
- Cold-start latency for low-traffic models

### Tuning
- Raise the threshold (e.g., `10000` = 10s) if your workload uses large models with inherently high latency.
- To alert per provider instead of per model, add `provider` to the performance stream dimensions and replace `BY openrouter.performance.model` with `BY openrouter.performance.provider`.
